topic: Plan the menu centerpiece for the medieval feast reenactment

scenario.topic: Plan the menu centerpiece for the medieval feast reenactment
scenario.opening_question: What kind of centerpiece best balances authenticity, visual impact, and ease of preparation for our medieval feast?

options.name: Roast Whole Pig on Spit
options.upside: Highly authentic and visually impressive with dramatic presentation
options.tradeoff: Requires long preparation and constant attention during cooking
options.concern: May be difficult to transport and manage at the venue

options.name: Elaborate Fruit and Cheese Pyramid
options.upside: Elegant and colorful centerpiece that is easy to assemble and serve
options.tradeoff: Less dramatic and less historically central than meat-based options
options.concern: May not fully satisfy guests expecting a hearty medieval feast centerpiece
options.best_for: Those valuing ease and variety over heavy authenticity

options.name: Stuffed Game Birds Platter
options.upside: Authentic medieval dish with rich flavors and elegant presentation
options.tradeoff: Requires skillful preparation and careful timing to avoid dryness
options.concern: Some guests may have dietary restrictions or dislike game meat
options.best_for: Those wanting authentic taste with manageable cooking effort

options.name: Giant Honey-Glazed Mead Cake
options.upside: Sweet centerpiece that reflects medieval flavors and is easy to share
options.tradeoff: Less visually dramatic and not a main course centerpiece
options.concern: Might not satisfy guests looking for a savory or substantial dish
options.best_for: Those prioritizing ease and thematic sweetness

shared_context: The feast is scheduled for next Saturday evening
Budget for the centerpiece is capped at $150
Exactly 6 participants will attend the feast
The goal is to create an impressive, authentic medieval centerpiece

personas.rejection_reason: The Mead Cake is too sweet and not substantial enough for the centerpiece I want.
